title: security: the review verdict is trusted by an identity every agent session can obtain, so ready-to-merge cannot tell a review from an agent's own write
author: minspec-sdd[bot]

title: pcompress: init at 4.0.1
author: gburd
body: Adds [pcompress](https://codeberg.org/gregburd/pcompress), a parallel compressor and archiver with deduplication, delta compression and encryption. It splits its input into chunks and compresses them in parallel with zstd, LZMA, PPMd, libbsc, LZ4, zlib, bzip2, or an adaptive per-chunk choice. It can also deduplicate, delta-encode and encrypt (AES / XSalsa20) each chunk. `src` is the 4.0.1 release tarball rather than `fetchFromGitHub`. pcompress builds its bundled, pinned lz4, zstd, libbsc and libarchive in-tree, and it applies its own patch to libarchive. Those come from git submodules, which GitHub's generated archives leave out, so the release tarball is the only archive that contains them

title: python3Packages.torch: fix MPISupport detection; add rdma-core to the runpath
author: ConnorBaker
body: Two commits. ### 1. `python3Packages.torch: put mpi in nativeBuildInputs for MPISupport` With `MPISupport = true`, torch builds without MPI support. Nothing fails: CMake prints `Could NOT find MPI`, sets `USE_MPI` to `OFF`, and the build carries on. FindMPI locates MPI through its compiler wrappers (`mpicc`, `mpicxx`), so they have to be on `PATH`. `mpi` was only in `buildInputs` (and `propagatedCxxBuildInputs`); with `strictDeps`, which Python packages use, that doesn't put the wrappers on `PATH`. This adds `mpi` to `nativeBuildInputs` when `MPISupport` is set. It also sets `USE_MPI` from `MPISupport`. CMake defaults `USE_MPI` to `ON` and turns it off when MPI isn't found, so with `MPISuppo

title: fix(server): isolate before-rollout jobs and show them in plans
author: PiquelChips
body: Before-rollout jobs were unsafe in four ways: - A job cloned its service's writable mounts, so an offline migration wrote a volume while the previous version of the service was still writing it (stop-first only protected the service rollout). - After a job failed, repair kept the prerequisites the deployment had already started or updated, so the old web kept running against database v2 and nothing ever repaired it. - Resuming a job after a daemon restart gave it a fresh timeout. - A new or changed job (a migration command) ran on deploy without appearing in the plan or the change list. ## How this fixes it - **Volume access** (REC-01). title: Bump the project version to 0.19.0
author: StevenJiang1110
body: The first commit fixes a bug in `tools/bump_version.sh`. Previously, the script assumed dependency declarations strictly followed the format ` = { version = "...", path = "..." }`. However, #3591 reordered these fields to ` = { path = "...", version = "..." }`, which caused the script to silently skip updating dependency versions and subsequently fail during Cargo dependency resolution. This commit makes the matching logic agnostic to field order and adds explicit error reporting if a target version cannot be found. title: mesh-llm, mesh-llm-native-runtime, mesh-llm-native-runtime-vulkan: init at 0.78.1; nixos/mesh-llm: init module
author: kleinbem
body: Adds [MeshLLM](https://github.com/Mesh-LLM/mesh-llm) 0.78.1, which pools spare GPU and CPU capacity to run LLMs across machines, its native inference runtime, and a NixOS module. **`mesh-llm-native-runtime`:** the llama.cpp build that mesh-llm loads at runtime. MeshLLM ships it as upstream llama.cpp at a pinned release tag plus its own patch queue (the Skippy ABI). - Its own derivation (no `overrideAttrs` of `llama-cpp`, per `pkgs/README.md`), with the same CMake setup and backend switches as `llama-cpp`. title: Remove embeddings, vector search and the reranker; search is FTS5 only
author: claude-code-dev-box[bot]
body: ## What Removes embeddings and vector search from the aggregator. Search is FTS5 only. The embed pipeline was already taken out of the deployment (nixos-config #346), because the llama-server backfill pinned ~12 cores. Since then every query logged `query embedding unavailable, answering from FTS5 alone`, and `aggregator_capabilities` still reported `vector_index: backfilling`. This PR removes the code that is left behind. ### Removed 1. The `aggregator embed` subcommand (`--catchup` / `--once` / `--seed-models` / `--reindex`) and the embed worker. 2. `core/embed.py` (the embed-server unix-socket client, plus the st/gguf backends) and `core/chunk.py`. 3. title: The NixOS module has multiple issues
author: wyndon
body: ### Describe the bug As seen [here](https://github.com/9001/copyparty/blob/hovudstraum/contrib/nixos/modules/copyparty.nix#L121C7-L125C9), some settings are set by default, and notably a pretty important one, `hist`, that sets the cache dir location. When the user change the settings, the values get overriden, thus breaks thumbnail generation because it then tries to write thumbnails into a .hist folder at the root of the volume, which copyparty needs write access to do so (not the case by default). title: AGENTS.md: add instructions for LLMs
author: 81reap
body: LLMs are pre-trained to look for a `AGENTS.md` when used in a coding harness. Nixpkgs has had an automation/AI policy but agents may or may not read it as they are not pre-trained to look for those files. `AGENTS.md` covers mostly all harnesses apart from Claude by Anthropic. For that we symlink the `AGENT.md` file to `CLAUDE.md`. author: jcszymansk
body: ## Summary On a Nix-packaged gc, the rig-scoped `core.control-dispatcher` never stays up. About 3 s after each start the reconciler marks it `asleep` / `runtime-missing`, the next tick cannot reuse or replace the canonical singleton slot ("slot stalled on its own runtime name"), the session is drained as `orphaned`, its bead is closed, and a new one is minted. The loop repeats forever. Long-lived control beads held by the dispatcher (for example a workflow drain) advance only in the 30-50 s windows, so a superpowers build stalled for 30+ minutes between tasks. Two bugs combine: 1. title: fix(copilot): github.com Copilot and copilot-cli are two runtimes under one name; HM instructions/rules are never read
author: higherorderfunctor
body: ## Problem `ai.copilot` targets **two different products under one name**, and the module treats them as one implementation differing only by config root. They are not. - **GitHub Copilot (github.com / IDE)** reads `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` from the **repository**. That is a repo-relative convention. - **Copilot CLI** reads `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` and `~/.copilot/instructions`, plus a process-wide `--additional-mcp-config`. Because the two were modelled as one runtime with a swappable root, the Home Manager backend emits the *repo* convention under `$HOME`, where nothing reads it. ## Concrete symptom — Copilot rules and named instructions are DEAD on Home Manager

title: features: say which posture refuses nonos-dev-attest
author: senseix21
body: @eKisNonos, a comment fix. The `nonos-dev-attest` comment in `Cargo.toml` said `nonos-production` refuses it in `src/lib.rs`. It doesn't: the guard there is keyed on `nonos-release`, and it has to be. `microkernel-desktop-gui` and `microkernel-setup-wizard` (and 53 other features) turn on `nonos-production` themselves, and the dev profile (`qemu-dev` in `tools/nix/config.nix`) is exactly desktop-gui + setup-wizard + `nonos-dev-attest`. A `compile_error!` on production + dev-attest would therefore break `make dev-image`. The real guard (`nonos-release`, which `config.nix:146` adds for every non-dev loader, plus the `config.nix:167` assert) is correct. Only the comment changes.

title: make nix detection faster
author: lhz07
body: Counting nix-user and nix-default sequentially is quite slow. On my MacBook, it takes around 120 ms (measured with `fastfetch --stat`). This PR changes the implementation to call `nix-store` in parallel, reducing the time to about 80 ms on my machine. It also removes the hash cache. In practice, the cache only improves performance by roughly 10 ms, while a cache miss (when the hash changes) can take up to 230 ms, making the overall behavior worse.

title: fix(bridge): end a formatting edit past EOF at the region end
author: atusy
body: ## Summary A downstream formatter answer is a `TextEdit[]` in virtual-document coordinates. kakehashi dropped the whole answer when any edit had an endpoint past the virtual EOF, to keep edits off host text beyond the injection region. bash-language-server (shfmt) answers with one edit from the document start to an "end of document" sentinel, `(2147483647, 2147483647)`. So a bash region in a Nix `'' … ''` string or a markdown fence was never formatted: ``` Dropped a formatting response (1 edit(s)): an edit extends past virtual EOF (line 5) and would corrupt host content beyond the injection region ``` A range end is a bound, not a location. title: feat(install): add env overrides and a test harness to install.sh
author: danmrichards
body: The CLI install script now reads RUNWARE_INSTALL_DIR and RUNWARE_RELEASE_BASE_URL. Without them, it uses the same GitHub URLs and ~/.local/bin as before. When the install directory is not on PATH, the PATH fix names the directory that the script used. The new installtest package serves a fake release over httptest and runs a script with sh in a clean environment. A test can then examine the output, the requests to the release and the arguments that the stub CLI recorded. A curl shim sends the default GitHub URLs to the fake release, so a test can pin them offline. The Serverless install scripts in RUNSERV-1266 must use this harness to run their tests without GitHub. author: lady-lemore[bot]

title: fix(activate): exit non-zero when units weren't applied, 4 when they failed
author: jeremy
body: `system-manager-engine activate` (and a profile's `bin/activate`) exits 0 when systemd didn't apply the profile's units, so a caller can't tell an applied profile from a half-applied one. We hit this running system-manager unattended: an upgrade loop switches, checks health and rolls back on a regression. On exit 0 it records the new generation as applied while the old unit is still running, or the new one has failed. ## What fails today All of these log the error, write the state file and exit 0: - **A job systemd refuses.** For example, a changed unit with a bad setting: systemd refuses to restart it, and the old version keeps running.
